text: After this you can inspect a requirement before using it in a design.

A requirement should express one needed outcome that can be checked. The teaching material lists twelve quality characteristics. Each helps expose uncertainty before design or testing. A complete set also connects needs, lower-level decisions and proof.

items: Write one condition for the system, without prescribing a solution. You should see: One outcome that a reviewer can assess. If not: Split combined conditions into separate requirements.

Check whether the condition is needed, feasible and within the right scope. You should see: A justified condition that does not assume an unproven design. If not: Ask which stakeholder need supports it.
Name the method and record that will demonstrate compliance. You should see: A requirement linked to a credible evidence plan. If not: Make the result measurable or observable.
Inferred: Replace "make the vehicle dependable" with a specific, justified service-availability measure and stated operating conditions. No numeric target is supplied here.

text: Check meaning, feasibility, and proof before accepting a requirement.
A well-phrased statement is not automatically the correct stakeholder need.

items: A requirement combines several unrelated results. A single pass result may conceal a failed part. Fix: Use one outcome per requirement.
A design brand is written as the requirement. It may rule out a suitable alternative. Fix: State the required behavior or characteristic instead.
